title: Mikie (C64) Reborn! 🎮 A Fully Procedural Tribute Built with GPT 6 Astra
author: Disastrous-Round-150
selftext:
Directed by Tee Jay and built with GPT 6 Astra, this is a fully procedural Linux tribute to Mikie (C64). Graphics, animation, music and sound effects are generated by C++ and GLSL.

1. We investigated the original game.

We examined a preserved C64 release using partial disassembly, recovered room-order data, gameplay captures and the original instructions. These findings guided a fresh implementation, with documented approximations. We did not recover or automatically translate the complete original source code.

1. We built a native game in C++.

The game uses C++17, OpenGL 3.3, GLSL and SDL2 for windowing, input and audio. It runs without a C64 emulator or original ROM files. A fixed 120 Hz simulation handles movement, collisions, enemies, projectiles and interactions independently of drawing speed.

The route covers the classroom, locker room, canteen, gym and playground, connected by four corridor visits. Collecting hearts reveals messages and unlocks exits. We rebuilt hip-zaps, shouts, distractions, stuns and hidden bonuses.

1. We generated characters and environments from geometry.

Code builds bevelled boxes, spheres, cylinders, rings, pleated dresses and rounded hearts. These become desks, lockers, lunch tables, characters and scenery. Repeated objects share generated meshes through instanced rendering.

The classroom follows my art direction: girls in pink dresses with pigtails, facing the blackboard, with red hearts rotating beneath their chairs. Walking, sitting, shouting and stunned poses use animated transformations. Even the lettering is geometry.

Room layouts are deliberately authored from the references; code generates their visual assets.

1. We added the modern graphics treatment.

GLSL formulas create wood grain, tile grout, cloth, metal, grass and brick surfaces. Directional lighting, softened 2048 × 2048 shadow maps, up to four-sample antialiasing and screen-space contact shading give the rooms depth.

Highlights, restrained bloom and tone mapping finish the image. Filtering fine surface patterns and adjusting room spacing kept objects readable from the elevated camera.

1. We built a procedural composer and synthesizer.

The newly composed score uses each room’s message to seed a repeatable melody. Scales, chord progressions and sixteen-bar arrangements shape phrases with answers, pauses and resolutions.

Six arrangements give the locations different musical identities: classroom guitar-like plucks, corridor bells, syncopated locker-room bass, jazzy canteen keys, gym dance rhythms and bright playground melodies.

The instruments are synthesized mathematically. Karplus–Strong synthesis uses a filtered feedback loop to imitate a vibrating string. FM-style synthesis creates keys and leads; filtered pulse waves provide bass; shaped noise and oscillators create drums and metallic tones.

1. We made gameplay part of the soundtrack.

Heart pickups sound in the room’s key. Collection progress adds answering chimes, while nearby pursuers add rhythmic activity. Footsteps trigger from distance travelled and change character across wooden, tiled and outdoor surfaces.

Throws, impacts, locker rattles, doors and the victory fanfare have separate synthesis recipes. The cartoon shout uses an artificial vocal pulse passed through three resonant filters that move between vowel-like sounds.

Stereo positioning follows the action. Music ducking, echo, DC filtering and soft limiting control the mix. The game loads no recorded music or sound-effect samples.

1. We refined the game through feedback.

We revised character proportions, dresses, pigtails, heart placement, room details and audio. Corridor staff now follow slower straight patrols, reverse before the end passages and leave those passages clear. Pursuit remains active in the main rooms.

P pauses and resumes; Escape exits immediately. We also added save/load, practice mode and visible respawn protection.

1. We tested the implementation.

The project passed 56 regression checks covering gameplay, objectives, corridor patrols, save/load and audio. We also checked builds, shaders, pause/exit input handling, and memory and undefined-behavior diagnostics.

1. We recorded a complete winning playthrough.

An automated controller observes the game and sends ordinary movement and action inputs. Enemies, collisions and damage remain active. The run collects all 105 hearts, includes four deaths and finishes with 43,100 points and one life remaining.

We replayed the inputs through the actual renderer and synthesizer. Each 120 Hz game tick produces exactly 400 stereo audio frames at 48 kHz, keeping sound synchronized even when offline rendering is slow.

FFmpeg encoded H.264 video with AAC audio: a continuous 4:43 playthrough at 1280 × 720, 30 fps, with 11 chapter markers.

An independent fan tribute to Mikie.  
Original game: Konami / Imagine.  
Creative direction: Tee Jay.  
Development with GPT 6 Astra.
